newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 19.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:

* Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will propose a sharp cut in conventional weapons in Central and Eastern Europe in an effort to soften Russia's opposition to the expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
* President Clinton arrived in New York City to try to raise more than $1 million for Democratic senatorial races.

* Zaire's government has dramatically increased the arming of Hutu guerrillas living among Zaire's Rwandan refugee population, threatening to spark another wave of ethnic killing as Zaire's embattled government enlists Hutu fighters to battle a Tutsi-led rebel army.

* Russia's failure to collect the taxes it is owed by its citizens and companies has increased government debt and fueled inflation, creating a major stumbling block for the country as it struggles with its economic woes.

* Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, the Army general who heads Mexico's federal anti-drug agency, remained out of sight Tuesday after his firing, and a search of three of his homes raised more questions about the country's anti-drug effort.

* Vice President Al Gore told the AFL-CIO Tuesday that the White House will consider how a company complies with labor laws such as those regulating overtime, worker safety and union organizing when awarding federal contracts.
